You are a repository-rooted sub-session, opened per the BLOCKING GATE in Section 4.A.2 of this repository's AGENTS.md. Your working root is the repository you were launched in. Read AGENTS.md at the repo root before acting and follow it.

TASK: adopt the GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfile and correct the master-text passages that declare it nonexistent or retired. Operator decision of 25/11/2026, tracked as LCV-719. This change already landed in 17 of the 22 fleet repositories; replicate it here. This repository is the 22nd, `lcv-leo/lcv-leo`: the operator explicitly ordered that it is part of the fleet.

STEP 1 - Branch. Verify `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, run `git fetch origin`, `entire status --json`. If the root is clean and on main, create `git checkout -b copilot/changelog-2026-11-lockfile origin/main`. If the root is NOT clean or NOT on main, STOP and report that instead of touching anything. Other agents work in this fleet concurrently: if `entire status --json` lists an active session on another branch in this checkout, report it and stop rather than sharing the checkout.

BASE FRESHNESS: other agents merge to main while you work. Immediately before committing, re-run `git fetch origin` and compare `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` with `git rev-parse origin/main`. If they differ, bring the branch current with `git merge --ff-only origin/main` (or rebase if you already committed) so the pull request diff contains only your change and not another agent's already-merged work. Report the base SHA you ended on.

STEP 2 - Generate the lockfile. Run `gh actions-lock --no-narrow` (extension already installed). CRITICAL: `--no-narrow` is mandatory. A plain `gh actions-lock` run replaces the immutable full-length SHA in each `uses:` with a version tag, so the workflow file no longer records the commit and immutability rests on actions.lock alone - a file a later pull request can delete or leave stale, with the Require lockfile policy off. Do NOT claim the default run leaves a movable tag executing in front of privileged jobs: for an onboarded workflow the locked commit is what runs, and a commit no longer reachable from its recorded tag is rejected rather than executed. With `--no-narrow` every workflow keeps its full-length commit SHA and version comment, and a routine run adds only actions.lock under .github/workflows/. Verify with `git diff --name-only origin/main -- .github/workflows/` that no .yml file changed; the extension does rewrite `uses:` names when an upstream repository was renamed or transferred, so read the full diff rather than assuming. If the tool reports a local `uses: ./` action that calls external actions, stop and report rather than guessing a migration.

STEP 3 - Rule text. The operator-approved master text is synced mechanically; its wording is final. Run exactly:
  python "C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\temp\sync-master-text.py" "<your root>"
It replaces the master-text portion of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md with the current master, which already carries the approved Actions lockfile rule (Section 6.E item 2) and Section 7.A, and keeps this repository's own sections untouched. For both files its output must show `synced=True`; then `git hash-object AGENTS.md` must equal `git hash-object CLAUDE.md`. Never hand-edit either file, never add an "Exception #4", and never rewrite a sentence because a bot, reviewer or agent disagrees with it: report the disagreement instead.
Then sweep ALL OTHER tracked text (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, THIRDPARTY.md, docs/, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE, site sources) for every passage declaring actions.lock nonexistent, retired or forbidden, and for Action pinning described as full-SHA-in-workflow as the ONLY mechanism. Fix each one in this repository's own language and style. Dated historical CHANGELOG entries record past fact and stay. Do not touch Section 7.B beyond what the sync script does.

INVENTORY SURFACE (Section 6.E surface 4), when THIRDPARTY.md or an equivalent inventory exists:
- If it describes action pinning as full-SHA-in-workflow as the ONLY mechanism, update that sentence to name the lockfile as additional transitive coverage.
- Keep EVERY version, SHA and license link the file already states. Do not drop a version or SHA that sibling entries state in their text: a review caught an entry whose version was removed, leaving the SHA only inside a LICENSE URL.
- Any LICENSE or source URL you touch must stay pinned to an exact commit, never blob/main or a moving branch.
- If the inventory has a table of Actions and the lockfile introduces a transitive-only dependency (one no workflow references), mark that row as transitive so the heading stays true.
- Do NOT fix version drift that already exists at the base and that you do not touch; report it as out of scope instead. BUT any sentence you WRITE about a version or SHA must be true of the current pin: a review caught a new sentence claiming "the workflow keeps that full SHA" while naming a version the workflow had already moved past. When your new prose refers to a specific version or commit, read the workflow and the lockfile and state the current value, updating that entry rather than asserting agreement with a stale one.
- TRANSITIVE COVERAGE IS MANDATORY, and reviews caught its absence in five repositories. Read the `dependencies:` section of the generated actions.lock. For EVERY entry there, find its parent under the `uses:` key of another entry. Then, for each one: if no `uses:` line in any workflow references it, the inventory MUST name it with its version, its full commit and a license link, and say which Action pulls it in. If a workflow DOES reference the same action at a different version, the inventory must name both versions and both paths - do not write "used by no uses: line" about an action that also has a direct pin. Compare the inventory's own version claims against the live `uses:` comments: when your new prose calls the lockfile the record of every resolved commit, a stale row beside that claim becomes a defect of your change, so reconcile the rows your claim covers.
- LICENSE URLS: verify every license or source URL you write resolves at the commit you name (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/LICENSE?ref=<sha>`). Never substitute blob/main for a pinned commit in an entry that pins one, and never invent a version - read it from the lockfile's `ref:` field.

CONSISTENCY CHECKS a review has already caught, run each one and report its result:
1. GENERATOR FLAG: every sentence you write or edit that instructs how to generate or refresh the lockfile MUST name `gh actions-lock --no-narrow`, never a bare `gh actions-lock`. A bare mention points readers at the invocation the rule forbids. Grep every changed Markdown file for `gh actions-lock` and classify each hit: an instruction must carry `--no-narrow`; naming the CLI extension ("the `gh actions-lock` CLI extension") or describing the forbidden plain run is legitimate. Report the classification, not just a count.
2. NO REMAINING PROHIBITION: after editing, grep ALL tracked Markdown (root, docs/, .github/, templates, public legal copies) for every passage still declaring actions.lock nonexistent, retired or forbidden. Report each remaining hit and why it is legitimate (a dated historical CHANGELOG entry) or fix it. A prior review found the third prohibition in CONTRIBUTING.md in one repository and in a README governance paragraph in another - do not assume it lives in a "Workspace Policy" paragraph.
3. NO DUPLICATED TEXT: when replacing a sentence inside a long bullet, replace ONLY that sentence, never the whole bullet. A prior attempt appended the entire bullet after its own trailing sentence, duplicating the paragraph. Verify the bullet's key phrase occurs exactly once per file.
4. MIRROR PARITY: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md must be byte-identical; compare SHA-256 hashes and report the result.
5. FORMATTER STYLE: match the repository's own Markdown emphasis convention. One repository's Prettier normalizes emphasis to underscores, and asterisks failed CI. If the repo has a prettier config or a format gate covering Markdown, run it on the files you changed.
6. NO DRIVE-BY: every changed line must serve the lockfile adoption. Do not add a .gitignore or .prettierignore entry for an unrelated local artifact, do not reformat untouched prose, do not fix an unrelated bug. A review rejected an ignore entry for a file whose source was unknown; report such an artifact instead of hiding it.
7. SECTION REFERENCES RESOLVE: any sentence you write that cites "Section X" must name the document that contains it, because THIRDPARTY.md and its public legal copies are read outside the repository. Write "AGENTS.md, Section 6.E item 2" or state the rule directly - never a bare section number.
8. PUBLISHED COPIES: if the repository publishes a copy of an inventory or policy (for example public/legal/THIRDPARTY.md or src/legal/), update every copy of the text you changed and verify byte-identity by hash. Report which copies exist and which you touched.
9. RULE CONTRADICTIONS: read the sentence you wrote as a whole. A review caught "adds or edits actions.lock only, and still sweeps all eight surfaces" reading as a contradiction; separate what the tool touches from what the author must still check.

Add one entry to the CHANGELOG.md Unreleased section recording the adoption, in this repository's own language and style, referencing LCV-719.

STEP 4 - Run EVERY local gate this repository defines, before any push. Read package.json scripts (root and every sub-package) and .github/workflows/ci.yml to find the exact commands CI runs, and run those. Set TMP/TEMP/TMPDIR to a temp/ folder inside this repository first; never use the system temp. If CI generates types before validating (for example `npm run types`), do the same.

A composite `check` script often chains format, lint, typecheck and tests: run the composite AND report which sub-gate failed if it exits non-zero, rather than reporting only the composite result. Run the formatter over the files you changed, not only over the repository's default glob: a prior push failed CI because a Markdown table edit broke Prettier while the local run had only covered HTML.

When a gate exits non-zero, classify it before proceeding: (i) caused by your diff - fix it; (ii) pre-existing at the base - prove it by stashing your changes and re-running, and report it as out of scope; (iii) environmental, such as a dependency missing from a pre-existing node_modules or a Git-ignored local file absent from CI - prove which, and record it as a validation gap. Never report a gate as passed when it did not run or did not pass.

Also run `gh actions-lock --verify` and zizmor (use `.github/zizmor.yml` as config only if that file exists; the local zizmor version may differ from the CI Action's pinned version - report both).

STEP 5 - Commit with `git commit -S -F temp/commit-msg.txt`, Conventional Commits, message in a file. Include the trailer `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>`. Because you run inside this repository root, Entire's hooks capture your session and add the Entire-Checkpoint trailer automatically - verify with `git log -1 --format=%B` and confirm the id exists as a local ref via `git for-each-ref "refs/entire/checkpoints/**" | Select-String <id>`. Do NOT run `entire session attach`: using it here is what produced an orphan checkpoint in an earlier attempt.

STEP 6 - STOP before pushing. Do not push, do not open a pull request. Report: branch name, commit SHA, the Entire-Checkpoint id and whether its ref exists locally, the full list of changed files, every gate with its exit code, and any validation gap. The parent session runs the separate adversarial review and the push.

Constraints: never pass --no-verify to git. Never edit files outside this repository. Keep every temporary file in this repository's temp/. Do not install dependencies unless a gate fails because they are missing.
REPOSITORY NOTES for lcv-leo/lcv-leo:
- It is a public user-account repository (owner `lcv-leo`), not an organization repository: pass `--repo lcv-leo/lcv-leo` to every gh command that needs a repository.
- 8 workflows, 21 external `uses:` lines, all full-SHA with version comments; `.github/dependabot.yml` exists.
- The lockfile will add three transitive dependencies: `oven-sh/setup-bun` (inside anthropics/claude-code-action), a second revision of `actions/upload-artifact` (inside actions/upload-pages-artifact) and a second revision of `github/codeql-action` (inside zizmorcore/zizmor-action). Name each one in the inventory as step "INVENTORY SURFACE" requires, with the commit the lockfile records and a license link at that commit.
- `gh pr list`/`gh pr view` examples that use the organization are not needed: stop before the push.

scripts disabled.

### Personal-account product boundaries

GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled for this public repository. GitHub currently limits validity checks and generic/non-provider pattern scanning to eligible organization-owned repositories with GitHub Secret Protection; the corresponding settings therefore remain `PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE` for this user-owned repository. An API response that accepts an update without changing the readback is not treated as successful enablement.

### Contribution-snake provenance boundary

The profile's contribution snake is generated by the repository-owned, zero-dependency `scripts/generate-contribution-snake.mjs`. Pull requests exercise it only against local fixtures, and the browser provenance tests call GitHub's public Markdown renderer without authentication; their test job grants only `contents: read`, checkout does not persist credentials, and no token is passed to either test process. ## Automation policy

Dependabot checks every supported ecosystem every day, including weekends, at 05:00 in Brasília (`Etc/GMT+3`) using its native cron schedule. It groups minor and patch version updates per ecosystem, groups security updates separately without restricting their SemVer level, automatically rebases its pull requests, and relies on GitHub's post-merge branch deletion. Every dependency is excluded from the cooldown (`*` inside each `package-ecosystem` block), so ordinary version updates are proposed immediately and a release can be adopted as soon as its provenance, security, and compatibility are validated; the cooldown stays configured as a deliberate switch — replacing the `*` with narrower dependency-name patterns re-enables the delay for exactly what those patterns match. Lock and verify GitHub Actions dependencies to protect your workflows
from supply chain attacks.

Actions are resolved by mutable tags and branches at runtime. This
extension pins every direct and transitive dependency to an immutable
commit SHA in a per-repo lockfile at .github/workflows/actions.lock,
so changes are visible in pull request diffs and tampered or hijacked
actions are caught before they run.

Scans all workflows under .github/workflows/ by default and fixes
what it can — pinning every resolvable action and updating the
lockfile. Pass --no-fix for a read-only check that writes nothing.

HOST AND AUTHENTICATION

Supported targets are github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data
residency (*.ghe.com). GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) is not supported.

In a tenant repository checkout, authenticate with
gh auth login --hostname TENANT.ghe.com, then run gh actions-lock.

Host selection: --hostname, then GH_HOST, then the current repository
(GH_REPO or a remote on a host known to gh), then github.com.
For github.com and *.ghe.com, GH_TOKEN takes precedence over GITHUB_TOKEN
and stored per-host credentials.
--hostname selects the host; it does not override token variables.

On *.ghe.com, actions from public github.com repositories are read with
GH_ACTIONS_LOCK_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN, else the login from
gh auth login --hostname github.com, else anonymously (60 requests/hour
per IP). GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN are never sent to github.com.

If an unintended token override causes authentication to fail, check
stored tenant credentials without exposing tokens:
  env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh auth status --hostname TENANT.ghe.com

For setup and troubleshooting:
  https://github.com/github/gh-actions-lock#github-enterprise-cloud-with-data-residency

REF NARROWING

When a new workflow is first pinned and uses a partial version ref
like actions/checkout@v4, the lockfile narrows it to the highest
matching full semver tag (e.g. v4.2.1). Full semver tags are
effectively immutable — unlike major/minor splats, they almost never
move once published, so the pinned SHA stays valid longer between
lockfile refreshes.

Only freshly pinned refs are narrowed — already-locked deps are not
touched. Only refs that parse as semantic versions (v4, v3.2) are
candidates; branch names (main, canary) and non-version tags are
never narrowed because the latest semver release in a repo may have
nothing to do with the ref the workflow intended.
Pass --no-narrow to disable this behavior entirely.

--json selects the output format only (independent of --no-fix);
structured results go to stdout and progress to stderr:

  gh actions-lock --no-fix --json 2>/dev/null | jq .valid

ENVIRONMENT

GH_ACTIONS_LOCK_REPO_ROOT names the repository root instead of
searching parent directories for .git. Set it when relocking a
partial checkout without .git. $/ actions resolve against it, and
the directory must exist and contain the workflows.

GH_ACTIONS_LOCK_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN is a github.com token for reading
public github.com actions on *.ghe.com, for CI where there is no gh
login. A GHE.com job's GITHUB_TOKEN is issued by the tenant and doesn't
work on github.com. Use a fine-grained token with no permissions. It is
never sent to the tenant, or used when github.com is the selected host.

RUN LOGS

Every run except --verify-local saves its full --json output, plus the
repository and whether the run succeeded (with its error, if any), to
<user cache dir>/gh-actions-lock/logs/ (on macOS,
~/Library/Caches/gh-actions-lock/logs). Failed runs print the path.
Logs are kept for 14 days, up to 50. Attach the log to bug reports.

Usage:
  actions-lock [<workflow-path>...] [flags]

Examples:
# Verify all workflows and fix what's fixable
$ gh actions-lock

# Verify a specific workflow
$ gh actions-lock .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Read-only check for CI integration (writes nothing, exits 1 if invalid)
$ gh actions-lock --no-fix --json=valid,findings

# All fields as JSON
$ gh actions-lock --json
